pr_body:
- While computing how many bytes we needed to write, we were returning the remaining number of window bytes (for both the connection and stream windows). Since window updates happen concurrently with the write loop, it was possible to miss and not observe the window update depending on when the update happened in relation to the loop observing this state. We now look at the current state of the connection window and stream window before we decide to queue or wait for a window update under the appropriate locks.


Fixes #41248
pr_comments: Is there anyway to unit test this? If it regresses we have some tests that become flaky, but it’s not an obvious break.
This is hard to unit test without adding lots of events that control exactly when things happen. Unit tests that are that tightly coupled to the implementation are no good IMO

review_comments: Why are we filling the array with 1s? Doesn't `new byte[16384 * 4]` fit just inside the 64KiB connection window? Apparently it's one byte too large given the test, but I'm trying to understand why.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/46554c9183e7ebdda173edd03038f19ea7ac75d3/src/Shared/ServerInfrastructure/Http2/Http2PeerSettings.cs#L14
Right, it's *almost* 64KiB.

It can go negative, right?
```suggestion
            if (_connectionWindow <= 0)
```

I think only the stream window can go negative. That's because `SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE` can be decreased after the connection starts, but that only affects stream-level flow control. The connection window can only be updated with WINDOW_UPDATES which cannot be negative.
Right!
